title: Trump's Medicaid Cuts Were Costing States Millions Before Anyone Even Lost Coverage
description_short: Trump's Medicaid Cuts Were Costing States Millions Before Anyone Even Lost Coverage
description_medium: States were already paying contractors millions just to comply with the administrative burdens in Trump's Medicaid and SNAP crackdown. That is an especially Trumpian form of damage: spend public money to make public help harder to reach, then call the resulting chaos efficiency. The cruelty is not just in the lost benefits. It is in making government burn money to rough people up more efficiently.
description_long:
CBS News, reporting on state documents obtained by KFF Health News, described the cost of changing Medicaid and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program eligibility systems to carry out the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. In five states, contractor estimates and initial changes totaled at least $45.6 million. Deloitte estimated nearly $6 million for Wisconsin Medicaid changes and another $4.2 million for SNAP. Accenture estimated Iowa’s Medicaid changes at $20 million or more. Optum estimated $1.8 million for Vermont system work. Kentucky’s initial changes cost $1.6 million, and Deloitte estimated Illinois changes at $12 million or more. Some figures were estimates rather than final invoices.

The changes address new work requirements, eligibility checks and other restrictions. The article said SNAP restrictions had begun to take effect, while major Medicaid requirements were scheduled to begin later in 2026. The Congressional Budget Office projected that the law would leave 7.5 million more people uninsured by 2034 and reduce food assistance for about 2.4 million people.

States contract with companies such as Deloitte, Accenture and Optum to operate eligibility systems, but the federal government pays most system-development costs: 90% of implementation and 75% of ongoing operations, according to federal rules cited in the report. The added work therefore carries costs for state and federal taxpayers before many of the Medicaid changes take effect.

title: Mass Social Media Surveillance - Political Dissent Monitoring and Algorithmic Targeting
description_short: Mass Social Media Surveillance - Political Dissent Monitoring and Algorithmic Targeting
description_medium: The Brennan Center describes Project 2025 as a plan to expand federal action against groups that counter election disinformation. It says the blueprint would pressure social-media companies over content moderation, weaken Section 230 protections and target researchers, election officials and civil society. The report discusses proposed policy; it does not document a system monitoring individual users or algorithmically prosecuting critics.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented comprehensive social media surveillance systems that monitored political dissent while using algorithmic targeting to identify and prosecute users who criticized administration policies through Project 2025's plan to weaponize technology platforms for government surveillance and political persecution. The systematic digital monitoring represented Trump's transformation of social media from communication platforms into surveillance infrastructure that tracked political expression while creating comprehensive databases of users who participated in online criticism, protest organization, or opposition political activities. The social media targeting included requiring technology companies to provide user data for political surveillance while eliminating privacy protections that had prevented government monitoring of digital communications, effectively transforming private platforms into government intelligence gathering operations. Trump's digital surveillance violated Fourth Amendment protections against unreasonable searches by creating warrantless monitoring systems that tracked political activities while using artificial intelligence to identify dissent patterns and flag users for investigation, prosecution, or retaliation based on their online political expression. The mass surveillance created what civil liberties advocates called systematic elimination of digital privacy rights through government monitoring that chilled political expression while enabling persecution of Americans who used social media to criticize government policies or organize political opposition. The social media surveillance represented Project 2025's vision of digital platforms controlled by government monitoring rather than user privacy, transforming online communication from protected speech into surveillance data that enabled systematic persecution of political dissent and democratic opposition through comprehensive tracking and algorithmic targeting of government critics.
subcategory: Digital Surveillance and Political Monitoring Systems
